## Slide 1

Learn To Row — Logic Model RESOURCES A coaching launch and eight stable training sculls Two qualified coaches employed for the season ACTIVITIES An eight-week beginners course each spring and autumn Free Saturday taster mornings open to the whole town OUTPUTS Ninety-six beginner places filled across the two courses Twenty taster mornings run over the season SHORT-TERM OUTCOMES Beginners can scull a length unaided by the final week Beginners say they feel safe on the water LONG-TERM OUTCOMES The club draws its membership from the whole town rather than one school

## Slide 2

Our theory of change Rowing should not be something you need a particular school to reach. The pages that follow restate the model above in the format the trust uses with its funders.

## Slide 3

Learn To Row — funder format Equipment: a launch for the coach and eight wide-beam boats for novices Staffing: a pair of coaches contracted for the rowing season Courses: two beginner intakes a year, each running eight weeks Open days: taster sessions every Saturday with no booking needed Places: ninety-six novices taught between the spring and autumn intakes Sessions: twenty open mornings delivered through the season Skill: novices complete a length on their own before the course ends Confidence: novices report feeling secure in a boat Reach: the membership stops depending on a single feeder school

items.text: A coaching launch and eight stable training sculls
Two qualified coaches employed for the season
Equipment: a launch for the coach and eight wide-beam boats for novices
Staffing: a pair of coaches contracted for the rowing season
An eight-week beginners course each spring and autumn
Free Saturday taster mornings open to the whole town
Courses: two beginner intakes a year, each running eight weeks
Open days: taster sessions every Saturday with no booking needed
Ninety-six beginner places filled across the two courses
Twenty taster mornings run over the season
Places: ninety-six novices taught between the spring and autumn intakes
Sessions: twenty open mornings delivered through the season
Beginners can scull a length unaided by the final week
Beginners say they feel safe on the water
Skill: novices complete a length on their own before the course ends
Confidence: novices report feeling secure in a boat
The club draws its membership from the whole town rather than one school
Reach: the membership stops depending on a single feeder school
Rowing should not be something you need a particular school to reach.
The pages that follow restate the model above in the format the trust uses with its funders.
